script:
Fatma: Did you hear about the student wellbeing survey our class discussed yesterday?
Hamid: Many pupils said they struggle to balance study time with rest and hobbies.
Fatma: Our teacher suggested a workshop rather than another lecture about stress.
Hamid: Who will lead it? Some pupils dislike sharing problems in front of everyone.
Fatma: A counsellor will introduce strategies, but nobody must discuss private experiences.
Hamid: When will the workshop take place, and how long will it last?
Fatma: It starts on Tuesday at ten and finishes before the second break.
Hamid: Our sports club practises then. Could we attend an activity afterwards?
Fatma: Yes, a smaller group can try the exercises on Thursday afternoon.
Hamid: I hope the workshop does not claim every teenager faces the same problem.
Fatma: The counsellor agrees. People respond differently and need suitable approaches.
Hamid: What will students practise during the first part of the session?
Fatma: They will plan a weekly timetable for lessons, family and sleep.
Hamid: That is useful. My brother often forgets time for hobbies.
Fatma: The second activity asks groups to listen without interrupting their partners.
Hamid: Will someone check whether we listen instead of offering quick advice?
Fatma: One student will summarise what another said and check its accuracy.
Hamid: What about social media? Comparing ourselves with friends can feel stressful.
Fatma: The class will discuss why photographs rarely show someone's whole experience.
Hamid: Could we ask questions anonymously? Some students prefer privacy.
Fatma: There will be a question box for general concerns.
Hamid: Will the workshop explain how to ask adults for support?
Fatma: Yes. It covers speaking to trusted adults and school professionals.
Hamid: Who will collect feedback after the activities?
Fatma: Class representatives will read anonymous forms and suggest improvements.
Hamid: I am glad pupils can share suggestions without being identified.
Fatma: The aim is confidence, respect and healthy habits, not judgement.
Hamid: I will attend Tuesday and invite my friend on Thursday.
